Clock sysvar read, write, init, and update logic with stake-weighted timestamp estimation.

# Purpose
This file implements the `Clock` sysvar for the runtime. It reads, writes, initializes, and updates the `fd_sol_sysvar_clock_t` account in the accounts database. The code sets the clock fields from bank state, including `slot`, `epoch`, `epoch_start_timestamp`, `leader_schedule_epoch`, and `unix_timestamp`. It also handles the special case for slot `0` by deriving the timestamp from genesis data.

The file also computes the stake-weighted timestamp estimate used to update `unix_timestamp`. The [`get_timestamp_estimate`](<#get_timestamp_estimate>) function scans cached vote states, filters out vote accounts that do not meet the epoch and vote-age rules, builds a stake-weighted median timestamp, and then clamps the result to the allowed drift from the proof-of-history time. The public functions [`fd_sysvar_clock_init`](<#fd_sysvar_clock_init>), [`fd_sysvar_clock_update`](<#fd_sysvar_clock_update>), [`fd_sysvar_clock_read`](<#fd_sysvar_clock_read>), and [`fd_sysvar_clock_write`](<#fd_sysvar_clock_write>) form the external interface for clock sysvar management inside the bank and account database.
